  "explanation": "The write-up infers from |E| < |V| that the whole multigraph G has no cycle or loop; this is false (e.g. V={0,1,2} with a double edge between 1 and 2 and an isolated vertex 0 has |E|=2<3=|V| yet contains a cycle). Only the averaging conclusion \"some component C has |E_C|<|V_C|, hence is a tree\" follows. The text then picks T as the component containing vertex n, which may be the cyclic one, so the 2-colouring and the sign expansion are unjustified. Since (3.1) holds for every nonempty J, replacing the choice of T by any component with fewer edges than vertices repairs it: a sentence-level edit. No other passage establishes the lower bound."
